filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether the outdoor seating can be approved under § 202.2(a)(7) or requires a Conditional Use Authorization, and whether the SUD expansion rule applies.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St, which has operated under a Type 47 license since October 2019 and was last approved by Planning in December 2019 as a permitted conditional use required to operate as a Bona Fide Eating Place, proposes to add outdoor seating in an on-site parking lot with alcohol service, limited cooking, and live entertainment. Ask whether the outdoor seating can be approved administratively under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) if it operates only between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. with seated areas only and alcohol dispensed only inside or by wait staff, or whether it requires a CUA. Also ask whether the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD expansion rule (§ 249.60(c)(3)) applies to a restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place, given that § 249.60(b)(1)(A) permits such restaurants to serve alcohol and § 249.60(c) appears to exclude them from the defini…

timeline_cost.notes: These are day and cost ranges for the approvals in the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Entertainment Commission permit, and Health permit to operate), assuming they are granted. The range is 4–10 months to approval and $3,100–$15,000 in government fees. The Conditional Use Authorization is the critical path: a CUA filing without construction typically costs $2,747 on the 2023–24 schedule (adjusted to about $3,150 by early 2023) and takes 120–300 days including pre-application meetings, environmental review, neighborhood notification, Planning Commission hearing, and a 30-day appeal period. The one outdoor seating CUA nearby (2323 Mission St) took 268 days from filing to approval in 2017. The Entertainment Commission permit (Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance) adds $612–$2,708 (2026–27 fees; earlier fees were lower) and 30–120 days for intake, referrals, posted notice, and a Commission hearing. The health permit to operate costs $470 (application) and takes 14–45 days after plan check approval for the pre-opening inspection. If Planning confirms the outdoor seating can be approved administratively under § 202.2(a)(7) without a CUA, the timeline drops to 45–120 days (for the Entertainment Commission permit and health inspection) and the cost drops to about $1,000–$3,000. This estimate does not include building permit fees (which depend on construction valuation), architect and expediter fees, or time to a denial or withdrawal. It also does not include the time or cost to obtain ABC approval of the premises modification or to amend the Type 47 license conditions, which may be required if ABC considers the outdoor seating a change to the licensed premises. Confirm the CUA requirement and the SUD expansion rule applicability with San Francisco Planning before filing.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); ABC licence, Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place); Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit; Health permit to operate

status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.

records_summary: 2351 Mission St operates as an existing restaurant with an active ABC Type 47 license (issued October 2019), and the records confirm restaurant use here since at least 1998. The property lies in the Mission Street NCT zoning district where restaurants are a conditional use, and sits within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District—however, the SUD permits restaurants operating as bona fide eating places to serve alcohol, and the district allows license transfers. The immediate block is dense with food and beverage businesses: 19 registered establishments within 500 ft, 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 46 licenses within 1,000 ft. The project adds outdoor seating with alcohol service to an existing licensed restaurant, which the pathway rules read as no change of use.
